review.notes: This is a truthful retrospective review of work already implemented before main introduced this gate. It does not claim prior review or passing device behavior. Cold and warm actions, real fold and accessibility remain subject to recorded evidence. On 2026-11-05 the cold-action trace exposed drain-before-JS-ack loss; DUO-009 was reviewed before implementing acknowledgement-based retention. Earlier prototype tests remain honestly retrospective. DUO-010 was updated after observing a native drain Promise stall; its non-blocking fallback and foreground recovery are reviewed before implementation. Permission-wait ordering was implemented during diagnosis; its specific regression test was reviewed afterwards and must not be represented as a pre-implementation review. DUO-018 and DUO-019 describe tests reviewed retrospectively after implementation; the new integration review must precede the actual migration. DUO-020 and subsequent driver/suite adjustments are retrospective WIP, not evidence of an earlier review or of a completed fold test. DUO-021 is recorded after its initial WIP implementation; the integration review must precede migration. DUO-022 is recorded after its initial WIP implementation; the integration review must precede migration. DUO-023 is recorded after initial WIP implementation; the integration review must precede migration. DUO-024 and strengthened DUO-010/019 tests are retrospectively recorded WIP; integration review must precede migration. DUO-024 active-state concurrent recovery assertions were added after WIP implementation, pending actual integration review. Duo posture tests wait at most 20 seconds for the measured hinge to reach the requested angle, per the driver 12.20 documentation; screenshots do not alone establish posture. DUO-002 now checks the unique session title after rotation; Duo posture tests wait for a stable observable window or visible modal control frame before asserting state, recorded retrospectively. DUO-025 records the compact navigation preservation fix and regression after WIP implementation; review must precede separate integration. DUO-026 and the DUO-023 outer-panel menu check are recorded after WIP implementation and require review before integration. Integration preparation from PR1810-derived local source cae4c446f3a5cfc8d8cca899d6f7eb9e5aaaf846 onto main 50fd32738d5f5171629a16d1f93e55aedc5d6a4c; this draft is not a review or evidence that original implementation was reviewed in advance. DUO-007 request-diagnostics.test.ts verifies the additional side-channel diagnostics in startFake (mobileapp/e2e/fake-serve/server.ts); the existing CT-HTTP contract remains intact and continues to map startFake. Independent review of frozen Q cae4c446f3a5cfc8d8cca899d6f7eb9e5aaaf846 against B 50fd32738d5f5171629a16d1f93e55aedc5d6a4c concluded with relay c04db94cf9a846c4a2095d3feb0e56c2 after review of earlier source stages and the final delta. The original implementation predates this integration review; this record precedes its separate migration only. Device, candidate and main checks remain outstanding. Follow-up review after run 42047638915: DUO-008 will verify a bounded hosted-only Appium idle lifetime long enough to retain a session during slow simulator preparation, with preparation timing diagnostics. DUO-001 retains its banner-tap assertion and captures the actual system surface when that assertion fails. No product wait or behavior assertion is relaxed; the cause of slow preparation and missing banner remains to be measured. The case objects retain their original reviewed behavior; the separately reviewed diagnostic follow-up above adds evidence without changing those initial acceptance criteria. Follow-up review from a055 simulator evidence: the outer 466pt root contained a 382pt workspace reader and 298pt detail chat because the shell and detail each apply a horizontal safe-area edge. Give each visible screen responsibility for its own outer horizontal inset, protect the regular sidebar and its reveal control separately, and exercise compact and regular state retention. Fold-reading identity must be checked after preserving the visible scroll anchor and revealing the intentionally auto-hidden header; the large-text scenario must navigate from any previous reader back to the list before selecting its session. Preserve all fold, identity, draft, interaction and accessibility assertions. The device remains to be retested. Independent Appium Duo guidance states hinge changes do not select a display and currentDisplayId controls screenshots and W3C actions. The a055 log reset that setting to null after unfolding, then notification long presses targeted the default outer display while screenshots were black. Each independent unfolded Duo scene/rotation case must explicitly measure angle, enumerate displays and select the inner display before actions, retaining all existing behavioral assertions; screenshots and actual native action evidence remain required. Follow-up review of run 42071592214: retain the native SafeAreaView root with no edges so iPad accessibility keeps radar-split visible without reapplying horizontal insets. While a chat reader is away from the live tail, use React Native maintainVisibleContentPosition to keep its first visible turn through content reflow; retain existing live-tail pinning, and verify the actual first visible message across fold. Verify Trace input has the exact intended text before folding, then assert it persists. Preserve all product behavior assertions and keep audit, scene-link and rotation failures visible. Run 42071592214 timed out the complete multi-step Duo rotation journey at Jest 120s while its outstanding WebDriver operation continued into the following scene-link case. Give that complete journey the same bounded 300s budget already used by the fold journey; individual waits, rotation, draft and session assertions remain unchanged. Native driver errors and any true product failures remain failures. In the large-text case, collect both display interactions and attempt each native accessibility audit even if the first audit errors; persist each error and fail the case afterward. Neither audit error nor missing interaction is counted as success. Run 42086224588 delivered a warm scene URL natively but the existing RN one-shot event did not reach JS. For recognized gtmux usage URLs, enqueue each scene delivery with an ID before notifying the visual consumer through a native event; drain and acknowledge once, retry after a missing listener or foreground transition, and keep other URLs on the RN route. Preserve guest/demo rejection and distinct repeated user intents. Native queue/signal checks and a fresh JS event test precede further device validation. Run 42086224588 showed a visible history prompt moved offscreen on fold despite the native anchor. Before width reflow, record a fully visible conversation turn and its viewport offset; restore that turn as its measured layout shifts, cancel on new user gesture, and never interrupt live-tail following or active text selection. Device reflow remains required. The outer accessibility audit also identified a small back hit region; make its measured target at least 44 points without changing its action. Run 42086224588 left WDA reporting the app not running after the warm background transition failed; the next rotation test queried orientation before launching its own app, so it did not execute its journey. Launch that test fixture before capturing orientation, preserve the warm failure and all rotation/keyboard/session assertions, and restore only an orientation actually captured. Conversation turns are windowed and can be replaced while the component remains mounted. When choosing a resize anchor, consider only identities currently mounted so stale measurements cannot steal the anchor after history changes; verify a removed visible candidate followed by a width change. Run 42099308533 warm action reached JS and matched its server but produced neither send result nor server write; the current delegate completion and receipt acknowledgment occur before the asynchronous send completes. Preserve the system response completion and native receipt until the existing quick-reply promise settles, bounded by the existing 20-second background deadline, without retrying an ambiguous send or changing default taps. Test duplicate arrivals while pending and native completion release. This is a correctness fix to premature completion, not a claim that it alone proves the observed failure cause. Run 42099308533 cold URL reached scene but visual tree stayed blank while background state ran. Safe-area-context Fabric source marks the initial insets sent before checking whether its event emitter exists; a missing first event is a plausible gate, not yet directly observed on the device. On iOS obtain a fresh, nonzero-sized current scene window and its actual safeAreaInsets on the main thread before mounting each visual provider, without a static initialWindowMetrics snapshot or fabricated insets. Keep background push active without a scene; retry when the scene or viewport becomes available, preserve fallback for old native shells, and allow subsequent native insets events to update normally. Validate real provider gating with null scene then actual scene and changing insets; separately require the cold Duo device path. Run 42099308533 still lost the visible turn during fold; record only numerical viewport/anchor/layout transitions under the existing test-only debug flag and save them alongside the failing screenshot to determine whether capture or later layout adjustment failed. Preserve the same fold assertion. The rotation test reached rotation and retained the draft but could not find the mode control: capture its actual failure screenshot and accessibility tree before cleanup, without changing assertions. The ordinary phone journey reached A0 through A7 in the final diagnostic record but the five-minute whole-test deadline fired before completion and could overlap the next case; allow a bounded seven-minute journey based on the observed hosted-runner duration while retaining every existing per-step wait and assertion. Source review after the 460 rotation failure shows DetailScreen intentionally marks its chrome accessibilityElementsHidden while the software keyboard is visible, so an immediate mode-control accessibility lookup is invalid. Keep the draft and keyboard assertions during rotation, then operate the existing keyboard toggle to hide it, assert the chat mode and exact session title, reopen and recheck the draft. This replaces an incompatible timing assertion with the same mode/session requirement at the point that control is intentionally accessible, and adds an input-state round trip. A duplicate delegate can arrive after the first response has completed and its prior acknowledgement was sent before that native callback registered. While a reply is pending, a duplicate must not acknowledge it early; once no reply is in flight, acknowledge the duplicate receipt to release any newly retained native completion without re-sending. Verify both phases. Run 42111899044 ordinary iPhone failed waiting for notification authorization. setupPush currently awaits the initial notification before requesting permission; a stalled initial promise can block authorization indefinitely even though native-drain and listeners are ready. Start those independent operations concurrently; do not let a late initial response act after teardown, preserve dedup and do not wait for permission before handling a response. The trace does not prove which native promise stalled on device, so add a bounded test with an intentionally unresolved initial promise and require a new device run. The same run captured a resize anchor at viewport y525 even though the first visible prompt was near the top, then corrected against that next turn; measure prompt position inside the turn, prefer the first currently visible prompt, retain fallback for promptless/very long content, and follow subsequent asynchronous remeasurements without overriding a new drag or selection. Preserve the unchanged Duo on-device assertion. Parallel startup must also survive a server-switch teardown while the initial response promise is pending: share one native initial request across bridge instances, let the currently live listener consume its result once, and never dispatch to the closed listener. Test the new listener receiving a late result after the old one stops. setupPush returns its teardown only after permission settles, so an unmounted bridge cannot otherwise unsubscribe when that permission promise stalls. Give the existing setup an optional lifecycle AbortSignal and have PushBridge abort synchronously on cleanup; a late initial notification must be consumed by the live bridge, not the cancelled one. Keep permission behavior and the existing async return contract unchanged; exercise a stalled permission plus unmount and late initial result. Follow-up review from run 42122509618: the ordinary iPhone authorization wait failed and the only captured app debug record predates that wait. If the unchanged authorization assertion fails, preserve the current debug events, screenshot and accessibility tree before rethrowing, so native rejection or a system alert can be distinguished from an unresolved request. The helper does not change permission state, timeout or success conditions; diagnostic artifacts use the existing task-only simulator fixture. Follow-up review from run 42122509618: the cold notification banner was displayed but WebdriverIO longPress attempted scrollIntoView and failed on an infinite point before the action could be clicked. Use the XCUITest driver documented mobile: touchAndHold on the actual visible banner element for both cold and warm cases, with the same 1.5 second gesture and unchanged system action, exactly-once send and scene assertions. A native hold failure remains a failure, not a skipped test or synthetic delivery. Follow-up review from run 42131652542: the screenshot showed turn 11 while the resize capture combined a later offset with earlier frames and chose turn 10. Preserve a user-scroll reading snapshot using the drag-end or momentum-end event offset and the corresponding measured visible prompt (or turn fallback); use it during a window-width reflow only while its turn remains mounted, retaining the existing bounded remeasure, tail-follow, selection and new-drag cancellation. On session change clear it. A regression must exercise a late non-user offset before resize, verify the original visible turn stays anchored, and prove a later user scroll supersedes the snapshot. Existing device fold assertion stays unchanged; this is a targeted fix, not proof of device success. Follow-up review of run 42131652542: the warm usage URL reached the scene and JS marked the usage sheet visible, but the recorded screen showed the iOS Open in gtmux confirmation covering the app. During the existing bounded wait explicitly accept only that exact system open-in-gtmux confirmation if present, then still require the real usage-close control to be displayed. Any other system alert is left untouched, timeouts and link/scene assertions remain unchanged. Follow-up review after run 42131652542: ordinary iPhone global setup waited for Appium for 180 seconds without a server or appium.log, and discarded child stdout and stderr, leaving startup failure unobservable. Capture only the spawned task-local Appium process output to an artifact and retain it on setup failure; preserve the existing server readiness wait, process isolation, cleanup and product assertions. Upload that diagnostic through the existing iPhone evidence step and use the existing CI guard; do not alter shared services. Follow-up review from run 42139938235: on iPhone 17 the notification initial request resolved, but the authorization request had not resolved or rejected by the 30 second failure capture; the screen showed no system alert. Under the existing opt-in debug flag only, issue one read-only checkPermissions query after a short delay while the request is pending, recording only authorization status and alert setting or an error category. Cancel the diagnostic on teardown or request completion; do not request, grant, deny or change permissions. This distinguishes current native settings from a missing request callback and does not treat either as a successful notification test. Follow-up review after run 42139938235: the first unfold stability check timed out while WDA calls were unusually slow; separate getLocation and getSize commands can also mix frames from different moments. Read the same element rectangle atomically using the existing WebDriver getElementRect command, retaining the same positive-size, selected-display, repeated stable-frame and timeout assertions. This reduces device round trips without inferring posture from dimensions or replacing any behavior check. Follow-up review from run 42151861243: the first fold-reading case stopped because WDA reported agent-row-%13 invisible even though the failure screenshot and accessibility frame place it on the inner screen. Require the real row to exist, verify its measured rectangle is within the current viewport, physically tap its measured center with the documented iOS gesture, and still require the exact target session header before any fold or reading assertion. This does not treat the screenshot, element existence or coordinates as successful selection; a missed touch or obscured row must still fail. Follow-up review of run 42158908662: the combined reading and keyboard journey exceeded its existing 300 second test budget while the selected-display driver was slow; Jest began the accessibility case while the earlier journey was still taking failure evidence and restoring the hinge. Separate the reading and keyboard draft journeys into independently initialized cases, each retaining the existing 300 second budget, real hinge transitions, exact session and reading/draft assertions. After keyboard opens, assert the draft and software keyboard on both panels; close the keyboard to verify the original session title and mode, then reopen to prove the same draft remains. Wait for an outstanding timed-out journey to finish its own bounded driver operations and cleanup before the following test starts, without changing product wait limits. Preserve evidence of timeout and do not infer a device pass from partial screenshots. Follow-up review of run 42158908662: the ordinary iPhone warm push did not expose the expected banner after the test pressed Home, so no notification tap or navigation was executed. The test used a fixed delay without observing that the app had actually left the foreground; a foreground delivery is intentionally suppressed. Before the warm push, use the same bounded queryAppState check as the existing Duo warm action journey and record the observed state. Retain the original banner lookup, exact tap and destination assertions and existing timeouts. This tests a lifecycle timing hypothesis and does not claim that it is the established root cause. Follow-up review of run 42165902359: on ordinary iPhone the cold notification was tapped, but the app was still at its launch screen when the fixed seven-second sample was captured; a later process delivered the pending response and interfered with the next case. Retain the original delay and all server, session and duplicate assertions, then wait within a bounded 30 seconds for the actual Detail back control before sampling the cold destination. Capture the same screenshot, UI and debug evidence if readiness fails. This tests startup readiness on the hosted simulator and does not assert that the slow launch is a product or infrastructure defect. Follow-up review of run 42174486679: the native outer accessibility audit timed out on a large transcript fixture; run the unchanged audit and real large-text tools journey on an independently seeded ordinary conversation, while preserving the separate long-history fold test. For warm action, preserve the existing 20 second background send check; on failure explicitly record whether foregrounding subsequently delivers exactly one send, then rethrow the original failure. Separate the enclosing driver journey timeout from the 20 second product wait and prevent timed-out journeys from overlapping later tests. For warm usage links, observe the new native scene URL after opening with a separate bounded system delivery wait, then require the actual usage close control within the existing UI wait; record both timestamps and retain exact system-confirmation handling. This exposes delivery and rendering separately and is not proof of a device pass. Follow-up review before implementation for exact 8079dcfe/run42182758196: Duo 7/9, draft journey completed all behavior after its 300s enclosing deadline, with repeated accessibility lookups taking seconds per identical element. Reuse per-posture composer handles and the stable keyboard toggle; keep long-chat fixture, all identity/draft/keyboard assertions, and existing deadlines. Warm simctl URL was handed to scene after 33.4s, then JS visibility in 14ms; WDA auto-alert handling and explicit alert polling overlapped. Use documented mobile: deepLink with bundleId for the warm scene handoff, retain native receipt and visible sheet assertions and bounded waits; cold simctl continues to verify system URL association. Do not claim this proves external-browser confirmation latency or physical-device/VoiceOver behavior. Reference Appium execute-methods mobile: deepLink (driver >=4.17, iOS >=16.4), within existing cloud 27.1 environment. This review precedes the following test-only edits; production code and permissions are unchanged. Additional pre-implementation review: 8079 outer native audit returned six DynamicType/TextClipped findings for three ConversationSelectionTextViews; inner audit was over the tools menu, so it is not a conversation comparison. Do not suppress those findings or label the audit clean. Strengthen DUO-023 by starting at normal text size, recording the actual short conversation text view frame/value, changing to accessibility-large while the scene is alive, asserting increased measured height and preserved exact text before both-panel tool checks. Record frame evidence and screenshots. Existing RN fontScale -> native document.scale -> TextKit measurement is reviewed, not yet established as the cause of the audit warnings; do not change production scaling merely to satisfy audit metadata. Correction after independent frozen-6163 review: inner audit was NOT moved; the earlier intended replacement did not land. The next implementation must explicitly close the inner menu before auditing and verify the committed ordering. Live frame/value proves neither complete glyph visibility nor all three affected views. Review before implementation: add Simulator-only, opt-in bounded numeric text-layout diagnostics in ConversationTextView, using UITextInput geometry without selecting text or accessing layoutManager (which could switch TextKit mode). Capture current document revision/scale, UIFont point sizes, sizeThatFits result, final bounds, selection rectangles and final composed-character rectangle; no text/links/credentials. In the existing Duo case match visible native TextViews by actual window frame, wait for current scale and stable geometry, require measured height and final line to fit the internal text container, and preserve both-panel raw native audits. This is diagnostic validation, not blanket VoiceOver or all-category certification. File-level history gate checks each mapped case against the first edit of that file in the PR. DUO-035 was newly reviewed after duo-fold already existed, so its current mapping correctly fails history. Do not backdate or weaken the gate: before migration, review moving the full text-size/session/tools/audit journey and native geometry assertions into new duo-text-scaling.test.ts mapped to DUO-035; original DUO-023 remains historical, its behavior is preserved by the new journey. Extract the unchanged posture implementation into setup/duoPosture.ts for both suites. Add the new file to the same existing cloud job and immediate evidence glob; verify the selector in existing CI tests, no new runner or altered timeout. Follow-up design review by the integration owner on 2026-11-06, before implementation: exact 6163/run42192884802 completed Duo 8/9. Cold simctl confirmation was accepted at 09:51:07, cold native scene at 09:51:20.959 and JS visibility at 09:51:21.488; the original 20-second wait failed, and its later screenshot shows Usage. Preserve this failure. Use documented mobile: deepLink without bundleId for the cold path so the default URL association is still exercised through XCTest; first require the app is NotRunning, then require a new scene-url-cold record and the actual usage close control within the existing 20-second UI wait. Save command/native/UI timestamps, retain warm receipt assertions, no increased deadline or production lifecycle change. Appium official execute-methods documentation confirms that an omitted bundleId uses the default application. Static review of the not-yet-run native geometry diagnostic also found that parent scrolling can change a window frame without relaying out its child. Add a simulator-flag-only opaque native-view accessibility identifier and match that identity plus measured width/height to the diagnostic record; retain the observed window frames in evidence, all current-scale/revision/UIFont/height/last-character checks and raw audits. If geometry fails, preserve its failure but still attempt both body audits before failing the case, avoiding loss of the second-panel evidence. These refinements are independently reviewed by the integration owner only; prior peer review is not asserted for this delta. Separate owner review before implementation: the exact 6163 outer large-text screenshot shows the transparent Collapse all label painting over conversation glyphs. MOBILE section floating controls already requires opaque fill, a visible border and shadow, while the full-screen section requires the control to remain independently floating without reserving a full row or changing the scrolling viewport. Apply that existing rule to the shared collapse/expand button only; keep the bar position, native transform, safe-area offset, hit target, text scale cap, content padding and toggle behavior. Update the existing full-screen regression to require opaque control treatment while retaining all current positioning and toggle assertions. This is a shared mobile control correction, not a Duo model branch; device screenshots on the subsequent exact head remain required. Owner review before a bounded VoiceOver journey: read the exact cloud-pinned appium-xcuitest-driver v12.20.0 execute-method-map.ts and commands/voiceover.ts. They expose public mobile: enableVoiceOver/disableVoiceOver/isVoiceOverEnabled and voiceOverMove with {direction: forward}, returning {utterance: string|null}; runtime requires iOS 27, which the existing 27.1 Duo job supplies. Use the same short fake conversation, select its exact session on the folded panel, enable actual VoiceOver, verify enabled=true, collect real utterances through bounded forward focus movement until the selected session title and Session tools have both been spoken. Unfold with VoiceOver still enabled and require both targets again. Each panel is limited to 48 moves and 90 seconds, the enclosing journey to 300 seconds; unsupported APIs or missing spoken targets fail and preserve evidence, never skip. Finally disable VoiceOver and require enabled=false before the shared simulator is reused. This verifies spoken focus reachability on the cloud simulator, not human listening quality, physical-device behavior or all accessibility actions. No dependencies, runner fanout, device pairing or production settings are changed. Follow-up owner review incorporating peer findings da687dc85debe572a4a659b1b0c413f7 on exact 3b7197: evidence-directory lookup and synchronous write must sit inside the outer restoration try/finally, so either failure still attempts VoiceOver disable/disabled-state verification and hinge/display/fake cleanup. Start the per-panel deadline before the first currentSpeech command, retain elapsed timestamps, reject every returned result and final success that arrives outside the same 90-second budget, and check before issuing moves. Await each driver command to completion and fail late responses; do not introduce Promise.race or leave commands running into cleanup. Add a lightweight fault-injection harness that executes the actual registered device journey with controlled driver/file operations: directory/write failure after VoiceOver enable must restore all owned state; slow initial speech and a move that returns both targets after the deadline must fail, while on-budget speech completes both panels. This validates harness contracts only, not real VoiceOver behavior. Owner follow-up review of peer R3 f6672135fbc0201293497a735d8b64f1: preserve R1/R2. On each settled panel, require the exact selected reader header and Session tools to be visible before speech inspection. Save currentSpeech only as diagnostic data; only newly issued voiceOverMove results from this panel may satisfy title/tools targets. Keep the same clock before all focus observations and late-result rejection. Extend the actual-journey fault injection to prove stale currentSpeech cannot pass and missing inner reader header/tools fails before inner speech inspection. The driver returns no element/display identity, so these observations do not certify physical display attribution without exact-head device evidence. Synchronize MOBILE English and Chinese wording: the bar remains transparent and floating, while its individual action has opaque fill/border/corners; horizontal padding 4 to 8 increases natural button width, not a pixel-identical layout. Owner review after exact cb6/run42203124701, before follow-up implementation: inner text geometry aborted on a stale element between name and rect reads; retain the original 20-second budget and all minimum-view/current-scale/unclipped checks, but reacquire a complete set of visible frames for each observation, reset stability after transient stale references, and never mix old/new sets. Missing identifiers, permanent errors or an unresolved set remain failures. Persist raw native records even when element sampling fails. A separate helper harness will use changing view identities, transient and persistent stale errors, missing records, clipping and expired budgets to verify the actual sampler; raw audit findings remain separate and unfiltered. The folded draft remained intact while the keyboard disappeared in the cb6 screenshot. No focus root cause is established: add bounded simulator-only opt-in native keyboard/editing/scene-geometry observations of first-responder class, window size/key state and keyboard frame, excluding text/URLs/credentials. Save them in the existing draft journey finally and preserve its keyboard assertions and 300-second limit. This is diagnosis, not a claim of keyboard recovery. Warm-link launch failed in XCTest before native app launch; retain the failure and capture setup failures within the journey evidence boundary without retrying or extending limits. Owner review after exact 1101/run42213150834, before the next implementation: default fake transcript timestamps are regenerated on each GET, while turnIdentity includes time. Freeze the default transcript epoch per startFake instance, preserving explicit world.transcripts, authorization, CT-HTTP and bounded request diagnostics. Add DUO-040 loopback HTTP regression with an advanced wall clock proving identical default messages retain identity across requests, a fresh fixture has a fresh epoch and explicitly seeded transcripts still win. This fixes evidence fixture identity, not proven glyph clipping. Reuse existing typeInto for the initial draft setup after a native first responder existed but one setValue returned empty; retain readback, post-fold keyboard assertions and 300-second budget. In the actual VoiceOver journey return from a preserved reader via detail-back before selecting the intended list row. Extend the registered-journey harness with a retained initial reader that blocks row selection until Back; preserve per-panel header/tools/new-move and 90-second contracts. These harness fixes do not claim real VoiceOver, keyboard or text clipping acceptance. Owner diagnostic review after 1101 ordinary iPhone authorization failure: WDA independently scanned both SpringBoard and the app every two seconds during the original 30-second wait, so lack of device polling is not an established cause. Preserve the same authorization assertion, timeout and production/native code. In the existing ordinary-phone CI step, after its single test invocation and before shutting down the simulator, collect a bounded 30-second read-only unified log query for gtmux and usernotificationsd (last 15 minutes) and the app native lifecycle trace, then return the original test exit status. Upload these synthetic-runner diagnostics with existing phone evidence. No permission mutation, extra runner, new device, retry or acceptance weakening; use the next already-required candidate device run to distinguish native notification service/scene delivery from JS readiness. Owner review of peer frozen767 findings F1/F2 (relay97fbdbbca049f97134ed47ad63ff2ad3), before implementation: bound only the newly added keyboard-evidence get_app_container synchronous child to5000ms and16KiB, with SIGKILL so a child ignoring SIGTERM cannot hold cleanup. Keep the draft journey300s, restoration and original failed assertion; log secondary evidence failure without replacing an existing journey failure, but fail a successful journey if required evidence collection fails. Execute the actual registered draft journey with controlled external effects and a real task-owned hanging child/output overflow to prove bounded recovery, original-error preservation, write-failure cleanup and normal evidence. Wrap the entire ordinary-phone Python diagnostic command in shell conditional handling, including mkdir/env/error-file failures, and explicitly exit the previously captured phone_status. Add stdlib unittest execution of the exact workflow shell block with isolated npm/xcrun stubs and filesystem mkdir/write faults, testing original0 and7 statuses; no real device/permission mutation or retry. Existing run42235158100 remains uninterrupted; later head needs its own evidence.

cases.description: native notification response queue retains a drained response until JS acknowledges it, while preserving identity, action, text, bounds and duplicate suppression
cases.setup: A Foundation-only native fixture with distinct response identifiers, numbered action and text; no user data or device connection.
cases.action: Enqueue duplicate and distinct responses, inspect the same pending response twice without acknowledgement, acknowledge it, then exceed the bounded queue capacity.
cases.expected: Unacknowledged responses remain retrievable; acknowledged responses disappear, duplicate identity/action is queued once, and only the newest 128 entries remain.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: a stalled native notification drain must not block the initial notification fallback, and foreground recovery retries retained responses without duplicate replies
cases.setup: Mock a native drain Promise that never resolves, an initial notification and an app-state listener; also hold a separate permission Promise pending. Use identified responses and a fake reply callback.
cases.action: Start push setup with the first drain pending, observe initial fallback, simulate foreground activation and a duplicate native response, and check a pending permission request separately.
cases.expected: Initial fallback proceeds despite a stalled drain or permission request, foreground retry retrieves a retained response, and shared identity permits at most one reply. If the initial notification is absent and the first drain stalls, a later active transition delivers and acknowledges the retained response once.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.expected: Duo acceptance verifies ad-hoc simulator signatures while native compilation remains unsigned and no production signing credentials are used. The isolated Duo job installs and verifies published driver 12.20.0 and WDA 16.17.1 for simulator hinge/display commands.

cases.description: Notification bootstrap runs before native safe-area metrics arrive
cases.setup: React Native renderer with isolated dependencies; the inset gate uses the installed provider implementation.
cases.action: Render the real JS safe-area provider without native insets, then deliver a measured inset event. Render the actual app with a ready identity and verify its push bridge starts with no native inset event.
cases.expected: Background handling starts before the event; the visual tree starts after it without remounting background handling.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: Widget URL listener stays registered across connection and guest state changes
cases.setup: React Native renderer with isolated dependencies; the inset gate uses the installed provider implementation.
cases.action: Change the current connection or guest state while delivering widget links.
cases.expected: One listener stays active, uses current owner state, and guest or parameterized links remain rejected. Changing the client retains one listener and uses its latest client; a guest-rejected link cannot open after switching to owner.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: The Duo simulator preserves selected conversation, reading state and input draft over real hinge changes
cases.setup: Named iOS 27.1 Duo simulator and isolated Appium XCUITest 12.20.0/WDA 16.17.1; fake server with long chat; no physical-device claim.
cases.action: Enumerate displays, measure hinge, interact with a long conversation and keyboard, close and reopen the simulator hinge, select each reported panel and capture screenshots.
cases.expected: Measured hinge reaches open and closed positions, the application window changes, the selected conversation and the same visible reading prompt survive, and the typed draft remains after fold and unfold.
surfaces: iPhone Duo simulator; physical-device and accessibility checks remain separate

cases.description: Trace search and Diff survive Duo simulator posture changes
cases.setup: Named iOS 27.1 Duo simulator, supported isolated driver and fake server with transcript and synthetic diff.
cases.action: Open the selected session Trace, enter a search, fold and unfold, then open Diff and repeat the posture transitions.
cases.expected: Trace keeps its selected session and search text; Diff remains open and both can be exited after posture changes.
surfaces: iPhone Duo simulator; physical-device and accessibility checks remain separate

cases.description: Cold scene activity includes the type and original activity expected by React Native
cases.setup: Standalone native Swift check with a synthetic browsing activity and URL.
cases.action: Build the scene launch dictionary through the same helper called by SceneDelegate.
cases.expected: The dictionary includes the browsing activity type under the supplied UIKit key and retains the original activity and URL; actual UIKit delivery remains a device test.
surfaces: iOS scene cold links

cases.description: Duo panels retain session and tools access at an enlarged accessibility text size
cases.setup: Named Duo simulator, supported isolated Appium driver, fake server; remember and restore the simulator text size.
cases.action: Set accessibility-large, use the session row on the folded panel, unfold and open the session tools; record screenshots and XCTest accessibility audit findings for each panel.
cases.expected: The size setting reports accessibility-large and the selected session and tools are reachable on both panels; save actual audit findings without claiming a VoiceOver or physical-device pass.
surfaces: Duo simulator text sizing and automated accessibility audit

cases.description: Scene links arriving after headless React starts survive until the visual consumer is ready
cases.setup: Native Swift synthetic scene inputs and a React consumer with a controlled native buffer; no UIKit device lifecycle is claimed.
cases.action: Queue URL contexts and browsing activities, drain before acknowledgment, mount the visual consumer, reject a guest link and retry an initially failed drain on foreground.
cases.expected: Scene URLs remain pending until acknowledged, the consumer opens an authorized usage link once, guest-rejected links do not become later owner intents, and foreground retry can recover the retained link. A stalled first drain cannot block active-state recovery, and a later duplicate is suppressed.
surfaces: iOS scene link handoff and app usage entry

cases.description: Compact list or reader navigation survives an expansion and fold
cases.setup: Rendered adaptive workspace with a selected synthetic session and controllable size class.
cases.action: Return from the selected reader to the compact list, expand and fold; separately select a session while expanded and fold.
cases.expected: The previously visible compact list returns after a round trip; an explicit expanded selection opens its reader, and a first wide automatic selection still shows its reader on folding.
surfaces: iPhone adaptive navigation and iPad compatibility

cases.description: A rejected initial usage link cannot replay after guest or demo mode changes
cases.setup: Separate isolated Jest test files start with fresh initial-link module state and guest or demo connections.
cases.action: Resolve the initial usage URL while guest or demo, then switch to owner without another URL.
cases.expected: A guest- or demo-rejected initial intent is consumed once; no sheet opens or usage request occurs after the owner transition.
surfaces: iOS initial link and cross-connection state

cases.description: A history reader keeps a native visible-content anchor without changing live-tail following
cases.setup: Render a conversation at the live tail, then simulate a user drag into history and a return to the tail.
cases.action: Exercise the chat ScrollView scroll callbacks and inspect the native anchor configuration after each user state transition.
cases.expected: The native visible-content anchor is active only while reading history; live-tail following stays active at the tail. Actual reflow is separately verified on the Duo simulator.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: A warm scene usage intent survives a missed event and is consumed once by the visual bridge
cases.setup: A native scene-link queue contains uniquely identified usage intents; the visual consumer subscribes and may transition between guest and owner.
cases.action: Deliver native availability events, including repeated events and a rejected guest intent, and inspect acknowledgements and sheet behavior.
cases.expected: Each queued intent is acknowledged once, a repeated availability event cannot reopen a consumed intent, guest rejection does not replay on owner, and unrelated URLs keep their normal routing. Native signal and actual scene delivery require separate checks.
surfaces: iOS scene links and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: A history reader retains a visible turn while the window width reflows
cases.setup: Render a conversation with measured turn positions, a history scroll offset, and a controllable window size.
cases.action: Change width, update the anchored turn layout in multiple increments, then exercise user interruption and live-tail behavior.
cases.expected: A fully visible turn remains at its prior viewport position across measured reflow; user gestures and active selection are not overridden and the tail continues following. Actual fold remains independently verified on Duo.
surfaces: Duo history reflow and ordinary-device compatibility

cases.description: Notification action completion waits for its asynchronous reply without duplicate sends
cases.setup: Synthetic native response completion registry and a JS notification action with a controlled reply promise.
cases.action: Deliver an action and its duplicate while the reply is pending, then resolve or reject; release native completion and exercise bounded expiry.
cases.expected: Only one reply starts; receipt and native completion remain pending until settlement or deadline; default taps finish normally and an ambiguous send is never automatically replayed.
surfaces: iOS warm and cold notification actions

cases.description: A visual workspace starts from actual current scene metrics without blocking background events
cases.setup: Real safe-area JS provider with controlled native scene metric responses and simulated inset events.
cases.action: Mount without a scene, deliver a valid current scene snapshot and later changed insets; exercise absent native bridge fallback.
cases.expected: Background work starts without a scene, no fake metrics are supplied, visual work opens with actual current measurements and updates when native insets change, and old native shells retain their normal provider behavior. Device cold-link startup remains separately verified.
surfaces: iOS scene startup, fold safe areas and old native compatibility

cases.description: Notification permission and initial-response recovery do not block one another
cases.setup: JS notification bridge with a deliberately stalled initial notification promise and controllable permission response.
cases.action: Start setup, resolve permission, then deliver the initial action or tear down before a late response.
cases.expected: Permission progresses despite a stalled initial response, the initial action is still processed exactly once without waiting for permission, and late callbacks after teardown are ignored.
surfaces: iOS startup and notification action recovery

cases.description: A visible prompt anchors history through asynchronous width reflow
cases.setup: Rendered conversation with measured turn and nested prompt positions and a viewport containing a partially visible earlier turn.
cases.action: Change window width, move the visible prompt and its parent over multiple layout events, then start a new user drag.
cases.expected: The first visible prompt retains its viewport offset as parent and nested layout settle; a new drag stops correction, and promptless histories fall back to a visible turn. Real fold remains separately tested.
surfaces: Duo reading position and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: Timed-out simulator journeys finish cleanup before the next case
cases.setup: A pending simulated device journey and an independent later journey.
cases.action: Let the first journey remain pending or reject while teardown waits, then settle it.
cases.expected: Teardown remains pending until the original operation settles; later execution cannot race it, and rejected journeys release the guard without concealing their failure.
surfaces: Duo simulator test isolation

cases.description: Visible native conversation text fits its committed layout after live text scaling on both Duo panels
cases.setup: Existing Duo fixture with simulator-only numeric text-layout diagnostics enabled; real UIKit text views and a running React Native scene.
cases.action: Change normal to accessibility-large while open, match visible text-view frames to native records at the current scale, wait for stable measurements, close each tools menu and audit the same conversation surface.
cases.expected: Current revision/scale records exist for visible text, UIFont points are positive, measured height and final character rectangle fit internal bounds, and raw audits retain every finding; normal parent scrolling is not mistaken for internal clipping. The selected session and tools remain reachable on both panels at accessibility-large, preserving the entire previous DUO-023 journey.
surfaces: Duo native text geometry and audit context

cases.description: Floating conversation fold actions remain readable and preserve existing navigation geometry
cases.setup: Existing React renderer full-screen fixtures with undefined, nonzero and zero safe-top offsets and native chrome transforms.
cases.action: Render and toggle the collapse control, enter and leave full screen, inspect the shared opaque control styling while retaining the existing layout and accessibility assertions.
cases.expected: The control has an opaque fill and visible border without changing its floating bar, safe-top offset, minimum touch size, bounded label scale, native transform or expand/collapse semantics. Device text legibility is separately checked by real Duo screenshots.
surfaces: Shared iPhone and iPad conversation controls

cases.description: Real VoiceOver focus can reach the selected session identity and tools before and after unfolding
cases.setup: Existing iOS 27.1 Duo cloud simulator, pinned XCUITest 12.20.0 and short fake conversation; VoiceOver initially disabled.
cases.action: Select the session on the outer screen, enable VoiceOver and move focus forward with the documented API, then unfold while VoiceOver remains enabled and repeat. Save actual spoken utterances and restore VoiceOver off.
cases.expected: VoiceOver reports enabled, speaks the selected session title and Session tools within 48 focus moves and 90 seconds on each panel, and reports disabled after cleanup. Missing/unsupported behavior fails rather than counts as a pass; physical and subjective speech quality remain unverified.
surfaces: Duo outer/inner VoiceOver spoken focus

cases.description: VoiceOver acceptance restores owned state on evidence failure and rejects late speech results
cases.setup: Execute the actual registered Duo VoiceOver journey with controlled device commands, filesystem faults and a virtual wall clock; no simulator is claimed.
cases.action: Inject evidence-directory and file-write failures, delay the initial speech or a focus move beyond 90 seconds, and run an on-budget control.
cases.expected: Every evidence failure still attempts VoiceOver disable and disabled-state verification plus hinge/display/fake restoration. Initial speech and late successful moves cannot pass outside the same panel budget; no detached driver command remains. On-budget target speech succeeds.
surfaces: Duo automation cleanup and timeout contracts

cases.description: native text sampling reacquires complete live observations without accepting stale, clipped or expired evidence
cases.setup: Controlled driver snapshots and native layout records; no simulator impersonation.
cases.action: Run the nativeTextLayout helper fault-injection tests.
cases.expected: A transient stale frame causes the whole observation to be discarded; fresh complete stable frames and layouts pass; permanent failures, absent identities, missing/clipped layouts and results outside the fixed budget fail.
surfaces: Duo accessibility evidence harness

cases.description: Default fake transcript identity stays stable across polling within one fixture
cases.setup: Start isolated synthetic HTTP fixtures and advance only Date.now; retain explicit transcript seeding and bearer authorization.
cases.action: Read default transcript twice across a clock change, start a new fixture and seed an explicit transcript.
cases.expected: The same fixture returns identical messages and times across polls; a new fixture captures its own epoch; explicit world.transcripts is returned unchanged.
surfaces: Shared fake transcript HTTP contract

cases.description: Draft evidence collection is bounded and cannot prevent restoration or hide the first journey failure
cases.setup: Execute the actual registered draft journey with mocked device/filesystem effects and one task-owned Node child that ignores SIGTERM.
cases.action: Inject hanging child, excessive output and write failures, and run a normal evidence control.
cases.expected: The command has5000ms/16KiB/SIGKILL bounds, posture/display cleanup runs, the original journey error survives secondary evidence failure, and an evidence failure after a successful journey still rejects.
surfaces: Duo draft diagnostic cleanup

cases.description: Phone diagnostics preserve the device-test exit status even when their filesystem operations fail
cases.setup: Execute the exact ordinary-phone workflow shell tail in a temporary fixture with stub npm/xcrun, real Python and no device access.
cases.action: Run normal collection, mkdir failure and log/error-file write failures with original test statuses0 and7.
cases.expected: Every run exits the original test status; diagnostic failures remain visible on stderr and do not turn failed tests green or successful tests into unrelated diagnostic failures.
surfaces: Cloud ordinary iPhone diagnostic reliability
